expectations.text: References the EDPB's draft Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation, adopted July 2026 (public consultation open until October 30, 2026), which will replace the 2014 WP29 Opinion 05/2014 on anonymisation techniques
expectations.evidence: "draft Guidelines 02/2026 on Anonymisation (adopted for consultation 7 July 2026, open until 30 October 2026; will replace the old WP29 Opinion 05/2014 once finalized)"

expectations.text: States the relative approach to identifiability: following the CJEU's EDPS v SRB ruling, the same dataset can be personal data in one party's hands and anonymous in another's, depending on the means available to each
expectations.evidence: "SRB v EDPS ruling (Case C-413/23 P)... assessed relative to the specific recipient"; "the same dataset can be anonymous for one holder and personal data for another"

expectations.text: Applies the 'means reasonably likely to be used' test for re-identification, rather than requiring absolute impossibility
expectations.evidence: "whether re-identification is 'reasonably likely' for that specific holder - not whether it is theoretically possible for someone, somewhere, with unlimited resources"

expectations.text: Uses the three re-identification criteria: singling out, linkability, and inference
expectations.evidence: "singling-out (isolating an individual record), linkability (connecting records about the same person), and inference (deducing attributes...)"

expectations.text: Distinguishes pseudonymisation (still personal data under GDPR) from anonymisation (outside GDPR), and warns that key-holding or auxiliary data defeats anonymity claims
expectations.evidence: "Pseudonymised data... remains personal data (Art. 4(5))"; anonymous data outside GDPR (Recital 26); "No retained key or crosswalk"; auxiliary-data assessment "where most anonymisation claims fail"
